content: I now have four distinct enforcement sites. Let me confirm the context of the `memo_service.go` first check (which handler it guards) to name it precisely.

All confirmed. Here are the distinct memo-visibility enforcement sites on the server.

h15.
Single-memo read gate (`checkMemoReadAccess`) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39 (visibility check at lines 55–66)
List gate — viewer-scoped visibility filter injected into the query in `ListMemos` — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:217–226
Comment-creation gate — parent memo visibility enforced before creating a comment — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41–43
Attachment-access gate (`checkAttachmentAccess`) — linked attachments follow the memo's visibility rules — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422 (visibility checks at lines 445–453)

Notes:
- Sites 1 and 2 live in the same file but are genuinely distinct surfaces: one guards fetching a single memo, the other constrains which memos a viewer can list (either via `VisibilityList` or an injected CEL filter `creator_id == ... || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`).
- The list filter ultimately compiles to SQL through `internal/filter/schema.go:162` (the `visibility` column mapping), but the enforcement decision itself is made at the service layer above.

That's four distinct sites — at least the three the question expected, plus the attachment path.
